Getting around

Metro for cross-city hops; trams and buses fill the gaps; ride apps for late nights.

  • ✓Metro ★Two lines (M1 north-south, M2 east-west) run every 3–10 min until midnight, later on Fri-Sat.
  • ✓BusAbout 200 bus routes and 30 tram lines share one ZTM ticket system. Validate on board.
  • ✓TramAround 30 tram lines across the city, on the same ZTM tickets as buses and metro.
  • ✓Taxi / ride appsUber, Bolt and Free Now work in Warsaw; taxis are metered.
  • ✓Rental carDriving is busy. Carry licence, insurance and registration documents at all times.
  • ✓Walking ★The centre is walkable and bike-friendly; no ferry needed in the city.
Recommended stay★ 2 nights (3 days)

Two nights cover the Old Town, the main museums and a food evening; add a night for Praga or Wilanów.

Climate

Temperate continental climate: cold winters, warm summers, and rain spread through the year.

  • ☀️Best time: May to SeptemberWarm days around 19–25°C and long evenings. Ideal for walking and outdoor cafés.
  • 🥶Cold winters (December to February)Highs of 2–5°C and lows near or below freezing. Pack a proper coat, hat and gloves.
  • 🌧️Rain all yearAbout 10–13 rain days every month. Carry a small umbrella or rain jacket any season.
  • 🌡️Big swings between seasonsFrom near 0°C in January to 25°C in July. Check the forecast before you pack.
  • 🌳Spring and autumn are mildApril, May, September and October are comfortable for sightseeing with a light layer.
  • 🧳What to packLayers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for cobblestones; warm boots and gloves in winter.

Landmarks 14

Must-see · 7

  1. 1

    Warsaw Old Town

    The reconstructed heart of the city, rebuilt brick by brick after WWII and now a UNESCO site. It is the essential first stop for any visitor. Go early in the morning to enjoy the squares before the crowds arrive.

  2. 2

    Palace of Culture and Science

    A towering Soviet-era landmark that dominates the skyline and houses museums, theatres and a viewing terrace. Head up to the terrace for panoramic views, ideally around sunset. Buy tickets on arrival.

  3. 3

    Royal Castle, Warsaw

    The former residence of Polish kings on Castle Square, richly restored with grand interiors. It anchors the Old Town and is a must for history lovers. Book tickets ahead in peak season to skip the queue.

  4. 4

    Łazienki Palace

    An elegant palace on an island in the middle of a beautiful park, surrounded by gardens and peacocks. It is a peaceful escape from the busy centre. Visit on a weekday morning for quieter paths.

  5. 5

    POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews

    A striking modern museum telling a thousand years of Jewish history in Poland. It is one of the city's most acclaimed cultural sights. Allow at least half a day and check opening days before you go.

  6. 6

    Warsaw Uprising Museum

    A powerful, immersive museum devoted to the 1944 uprising, with moving exhibits and artefacts. It is essential for understanding the city's modern identity. Book timed tickets in advance.

  7. 7

    Wilanów Palace

    A baroque royal palace with formal gardens on the city's southern edge. It makes a rewarding half-day trip away from the centre. Take a bus or taxi and go early to beat the crowds.

    Day trips from Warsaw

    Toruń · 2 h 13 by train

    ★★★★☆ · Full day · 259 km from Warsaw

    Best way: Direct intercity trains reach Toruń Główny in 2h 13m, faster than the 3h bus, and the old town is a short walk or local bus from the station.

    Direct intercity trains from Warszawa Centralna reach Toruń Główny in roughly 2.5 to 3 hours; the old town is a short walk or local bus from the station.

    • Train ★2 h 13 · from $29-$55
    • Bus3 h 00
    • Car2 h 43 · taxi ≈ 790 PLN

    What to see

    • Medieval Old Town and Town Hall
    • Copernicus House Museum
    • Gothic Cathedral of SS. John
    • Vistula riverfront

    1 landmark quest to check off here

    Good to know

    • Book intercity tickets ahead, especially on weekends
    • The old town is a UNESCO-listed Gothic gem, best explored on foot
    • Allow a full day to see the cathedral, town hall and Copernicus sights

    Łódź · 58 min by train

    ★★★☆☆ · Full day · 136 km from Warsaw

    Best way: Frequent direct trains take just 58m, far quicker than the 1h 40m bus, and Łódź Fabryczna station is close to the centre.

    Frequent direct trains from Warszawa Centralna to Łódź Fabryczna take about 1.5 hours, with the station close to the city centre.

    • Train ★58 min · from €26
    • Bus1 h 40 · from $8-$13
    • Car1 h 32 · taxi ≈ 420 PLN

    What to see

    • Piotrkowska Street
    • Manufaktura complex
    • Poznański Palace
    • Central Museum of Textiles

    Good to know

    • Piotrkowska Street is the main draw, best on a warm day
    • Check train times for the last service back to Warsaw
    • Many museums close on Mondays

    Times and prices are typical one-way estimates (train and bus: Omio / Rome2Rio route data; taxi: local tariff × road distance, tolls extra). Exact prices are on the booking page.

    Build my plan

    Swap in instead

    • Add a half-day in Praga: cross the river for street art, the zoo and the old bazaar area.
    • Day trip to Wilanów Palace and its gardens, south of the city; check opening hours on the day.
    • History fans can spend a full afternoon at the POLIN Museum and the Warsaw Uprising Museum.

    Getting around

    • Two metro lines (M1 north-south, M2 east-west) run every 3-10 min until midnight, later on Fri-Sat.
    • About 200 bus routes and 30 tram lines share one ZTM ticket system.
    • Buy tickets in machines, on some trams, or via the Jakdojade app; validate on board.
    • Ride apps Uber, Bolt and Free Now work in Warsaw; taxis are metered.
    • Driving is busy; carry licence, insurance and registration documents at all times.
    • The centre is walkable and bike-friendly; no ferry needed in the city.

    Where to stay

    • Śródmieście · ≈ PLN 220–550 a night
      Central and walkable. Close to the main station, the Palace of Culture and both metro lines.
    • Old Town · ≈ PLN 250–600 a night
      Stay inside the rebuilt UNESCO square. Pretty at night, but quieter and pricier for food.
    • Wola · ≈ PLN 180–420 a night
      Modern towers and the Rising Museum. Good value and fast metro links to the centre.
    • Mokotów · ≈ PLN 170–400 a night
      Green, calm and cheaper. Good for longer stays; a tram or metro ride to the sights.

    Food & drink

    • Try Polish classics: pierogi (dumplings), żurek (sour rye soup) and bigos (cabbage stew).
    • Milk bars (bar mleczny) serve cheap home-style meals, often under 25 PLN. Look for them near the centre.
    • Eat a zapiekanka on the street, and save room for pączki (doughnuts) at a bakery.
    • Book dinner in Śródmieście or Praga for the widest choice; prices vary, so check menus first.
    • Drink local: Polish beer and vodka are common. Tap water is safe to drink.

    Tips

    1. Buy standard ZTM tickets or use mobile apps like Jakdojade for all public transit
    2. The Old Town is entirely reconstructed but incredibly authentic and beautiful
    3. Milk bars (bar mleczny) offer excellent and highly affordable traditional Polish food
    4. Tap water is generally safe to drink
    5. Do not cross the street on a red light, even if it's clear — fines are strictly enforced

    Souvenirs

    Chopin Chocolate

    PLN 75–90263 g tin · shop prices

    A Warsaw chocolate brand, and its packs often feature piano and Chopin designs that link the sweets to the city's most famous composer.

    Where: E. Wedel, Szpitalna Street
    Pick the piano-design pack if you want something that clearly says Warsaw.

    Bolesławiec Pottery

    PLN 70–1801 small cup · estimate

    Hand-painted stoneware from Bolesławiec in southwestern Poland, a regional craft that is also sold in Warsaw shops.

    Where: Ceramika Bolesławiecka specialty shop, Warsaw
    Buy one small cup first to check the glaze and painting before choosing larger pieces.
